 ACA health insurance rates released for 2027 open enrollment
 Posted on October 30, 2026 
 by Mike Fuhrman 
 Special to IFN 
 RALEIGH — Approved rates for the 2027 Affordable Care Act policies have been released.
 For those in North Carolina who have individual ACA coverage, increases in premiums will range from 8.35% to 27.36%. Increases for small group policies will range from 18.78% to 19.54%.
 Open enrollment for 2027 ACA policies runs from November 1, 2026, to January 15, 2027. Signing up by December 15, 2026, ensures your coverage will begin on January 1, 2027. Coverage for those signing up after December 15, 2026, will begin on February 1, 2027.
 “While ACA increases are way less than last year’s, the increased cost of claims, healthcare and prescription drugs continues pushing monthly premiums higher,” Insurance Commissioner Mike Causey said. “It’s important that people buying ACA health insurance go to www.healthcare.gov , research options and choose the plans that work best for them and their families.”
 Causey urges consumers needing help navigating their options to contact a consumer specialist at the Department of Insurance at 855-408-1212 weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
 In addition to ACA plans, Commissioner Causey suggested North Carolinians consider other options:
 Enroll in job-based coverage. This may be the most affordable option for many individuals and families. If you’re employed and your employer offers health benefits, you may qualify to enroll in health insurance through your employer, even if you have declined this coverage in the past. You may also be able to enroll in coverage through your spouse’s employer or, if you are younger than 26, through your parents’ employer.
 Enroll in a plan through a private insurer. You may purchase coverage through an agent or broker, or directly from a health insurance company. You may find plans that cost less than an ACA plan. Just be sure they provide the coverage you need.
Enroll in a student health plan. If you are younger than 30 and enrolled in school, you may be eligible for a student health plan. Contact your school to explore this option.
 “Whatever you do, it is important for you to maintain health insurance coverage,” Commissioner Causey said.

 It is a travesty health insurance costs so much. No matter what type of insurance individuals/families are enrolled in, we pay more in premiums and get less in benefits. I believe a few things may contribute to this problem.

Told healthcare would be more affordable. Not true. The number of people on the ACA plans grew exponentially to include people who shouldn’t have been eligible. Less for our poorest of people.
 I was appalled when I read about the huge Medicaid fraud in NC. Those responsible for overseeing fraud in NC should lose their jobs. The fraudsters sent to prison! Again, our poorest have been affected. Taking more of our tax dollars or income to pay for rampant fraud is tragic. 
 It’s my understanding Congress refused to give physicians higher rates for Medicare patients. Again. Yet, these physicians pay higher prices every year! Physicians have to hire workers just to process paperwork for insurance companies, especially pre-authorizations. Many including benefits. Adding to insurance costs. Not to mention the added physician stress.
 Why are prescription drugs going higher? It was my understanding this Administration made deals with big pharmaceutical companies to give us the rates they charge other countries. The fact Americans have paid so much more for the same drugs all these years compared to Europe is sickening. 
 Needless to say, these corporate insurance companies are making big money off our backs! How about our politicians holding THEM accountable!
